program.title: GENIUS Act implementation tracker
program.thesis: Break the GENIUS Act and its four implementing rules into individual requirements, classify each by area, who it binds, and how prescriptive it is, then pair every statutory requirement with same-area provisions in the rules. Coverage by area shows where rulemaking has caught up and where the statute still stands alone.

unit.rationale: Duty-, permission-, and definition-bearing paragraphs from the statute and the regulatory text of the four rules (preamble discussion, comment requests, and impact analyses excluded by section role).

doc_notes.note: The GENIUS Act, enacted July 18, 2025, is the federal statute for payment stablecoins. It limits U.S. issuance to permitted payment stablecoin issuers and directs Treasury, the Federal Reserve, and other regulators to issue implementing rules.
Treasury proposed rule published August 18, 2026, implementing GENIUS Act provisions on the issuance, offer, and sale of payment stablecoins in the United States.
Federal Reserve Board proposed rule published September 29, 2026, implementing the Board's responsibilities under the GENIUS Act.
Federal Reserve Board proposed rule published September 29, 2026, on application procedures for Board-supervised insured depository institutions seeking approval to issue payment stablecoins.
Treasury final rule published September 30, 2026, setting forms and procedures for the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee's review of state certifications under the GENIUS Act.

Capital, liquidity, or risk-management standards

Disclosures, reports, attestations, or audits
Supervision, examination, enforcement, or penalties
Foreign payment stablecoin issuers, comparability, or reciprocity
State-level regulatory regimes and their certification
Custody of customer assets, insolvency priority, or consumer protection
Marketing, naming, or representations about stablecoins
Definitions or scope of coverage
Something else

nodes.label: Prescriptiveness
nodes.question: How specific is this provision?
levels: Principle: states a goal or general standard
Highly specific: numbers, lists, forms, or deadlines
nodes.why: Statutes set principles; rules should add specifics. This measures it.

B has nothing to do with A
